decisions.reason: As a design-led decorative line extension, this devoré fabric is relatively fashion-sensitive, and without clear evidence of continued prominence the firm would likely reallocate shelf and sampling capacity if it fell short of rising aspirations in a growing market.

This transparent burnout decorative fabric is close to the core offer but also trend-driven, so a medium-sized textile firm with active collection management would be somewhat more likely to discontinue it if repeat orders did not clearly justify warehouse and presentation resources.

Because this burnout decorative fabric is an incremental decorative variant rather than a distinctive new capability, management would likely drop it if its performance was merely mediocre relative to comparable products and internal aspirations.

A velour-like upholstery fabric fits the firm’s established upholstery business well and is more likely to benefit from reorder continuity and stocked availability, so the firm would tend to retain it unless results were clearly disappointing.

The flame-retardant plain inbetween fabric serves a practical, service-oriented niche and strengthens the firm’s dependable supply proposition, making it relatively likely to be kept given the firm’s slack and customer-service model.

This polyester lining fabric with satin sheen is a functional adjacent product that can complement made-to-measure sewing and sampling, so management would lean toward keeping it unless demand proved persistently weak.
